match.failure_attacks_route_basis: The main risk is a one-sided Madrid control win, not loss of the Madrid scoring route.
match.material_suppression_basis: No current all-route suppression is verified.

match.activation_basis: AEK's last two UCL matches opened into multi-goal games and Madrid have scored four in consecutive league-phase fixtures with their main attacking core still projected to start.
match.board_state_basis: Strong self-funding Madrid carrier, high AEK leakage and same-competition upper-tail evidence make this a high-quality goal candidate.

matches.qualification_state: Liverpool enter on a perfect nine points from three and top-eight pace. Fenerbahce have two points from three and are outside the stronger qualification positions, so Fener have much greater recovery pressure while Liverpool retain top-eight/seeding value.
matches.simultaneous_results_note: Matchday 4 is not the final simultaneous league-phase round.
matches.match_context_basis: Normal Champions League travel is present but no verified rest/fatigue asymmetry is large enough to alter the football grades.

matches.main_failure: Liverpool's injury list can reduce control and Fener can still fail to score, but Liverpool have conceded in every UCL game while scoring at least two in all three.
matches.supported_line_basis: Liverpool's strong carrier, Fener's usable home reply and repeated same-competition high totals protect G3 and support a separate G4 path; the compiler remains authoritative.
matches.carrier_self_fund_basis: Liverpool scored six at LASK and four against Villarreal, establishing a current self-funding three-plus route.
matches.independent_upper_tail_basis: Liverpool's last two UCL games produced nine and seven goals; Fener's three UCL matches produced two, six and four. Same-competition evidence supports continued scoring through goal four.
matches.upper_tail_transferability_basis: The strongest high-total evidence is from the current Champions League league phase, not domestic mismatches.
matches.upper_tail_comparable_context_basis: Four of the six combined UCL matches have reached at least four goals, including Liverpool's last two and Fener's last two.
matches.failure_attacks_route_basis: The principal risk is Fener failing to contribute, but Liverpool's carrier remains strong enough that the route itself is not broken.
matches.material_suppression_basis: No verified all-route suppression exists; current injuries cap XI robustness at MEDIUM but do not erase either route.
matches.g3_current_structure_basis: Liverpool have scored 12 in three UCL matches and conceded in all three; Fener have scored in two of three and must chase points at home.
matches.activation_basis: Liverpool's last two Champions League games became extreme multi-goal contests, while Fener's last two produced six and four total goals and their table position gives them little reason to sit on a draw.
matches.board_state_basis: Strong Liverpool carrier, live Fener reply and high same-competition tail make this a high-quality goal candidate.
